parole.significato: akja (larger pulk); traditionally used by the Sami, drawn by reindeer or a skier
parole.testo: From older Finnish akkia or older Sami akio, akje (compare Karelian ahkivo), from a Proto-Uralic *aškɜ, or Proto-Norse *ᚨᚲᛃᛟ (*akjō), corresponding to Swedish äcka, Icelandic ekja (“driving, fording”), to the root ak (Swedish åk), “drive, ford, ride”. Borrows include: German Akia, Akja, Ackja; Engli

parole.significato: pesäpallo (sport developed in Finland in 1920's based largely on baseball)
parole.testo: bo + boll; calque of Finnish pesäpallo.

parole.significato: a clothes peg
parole.testo: Compound of byk (“laundry”) + pojke (“boy”). Calque of Finnish pyykkipoika.

parole.significato: detached house
parole.testo: Calque of Finnish omakotitalo.

parole.significato: an accordion
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish haitari (“accordion”). By surface analysis, "hajder."

parole.significato: a member of the Swedish-speaking population in Finland (often in positive self-reference)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish hurri. By surface analysis, hurra (“cheer, hooray”) + -are (“-er”).

parole.significato: good, honest, stand-up, companionable
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish hyvin (“well”), from Finnish hyvä (“good”).

parole.significato: to rush (to perform a task with great haste)
parole.testo: < Finnish hosua (“to rush”)

parole.significato: fun, nice
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish kiva.

parole.significato: to die
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish kuolla. Compare ta kål på.

parole.significato: money
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish kova, from expressions like kova raha (“hard money”).

parole.significato: hangover
parole.testo: From krapula + -is, from Finnish krapula, from Latin crapula.

parole.significato: a boot (heavy shoe with a fairly short shaft)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish kenkä, from Proto-Finnic *kenkä.

parole.significato: a Lapp, a Sami person; a person of the Sami people
parole.testo: From Old Swedish lapper; compare Icelandic lappir pl; probably of Finnish origin; compare Finnish lappalainen (“Lap”), after Lappi (“Lapland”), older Finnish also lapp; original meaning unknown.

parole.significato: mämmi
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish mämmi.

parole.significato: a milk carton
parole.testo: Compound of mjölk + tölk. Calque of Finnish maitotölkki.

parole.significato: vendace (Coregonus albula)
parole.testo: Borrowing from Finnish muikku.

parole.significato: to doze off, to nod off
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish nukkua or nuokahtaa.

parole.significato: palsa; a turf hillock with a frozen core
parole.testo: From Finnish palsa, from Lule Sami balsa.

parole.significato: One of a pair of ski boots.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish pieksu.

parole.significato: a boy (young male)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Swedish poika, from Finnish poika.

parole.significato: a pulk (small boat-like Sami transport sled)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish pulkka, from Sami puhlke.

parole.significato: a Finnish-style log cabin without a chimney, but with a fireplace
parole.testo: From Old Swedish pyrte, borrowed from Finnish pirtti (“cabin, cottage”) with rounding of the vowel following a labial and preceding a coronal sonorant. Cf. mynta (“mint”).

parole.significato: nonsense (talk)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnish rapakalja. Shifts in sense seems to have gone from "beer" (as in Finnish) via "gruel" (a sense not attested in Finnish) to "mess", to current sense.

parole.significato: a dryer, a kiln to dry corn; a traditional Finnish/Scandinavian wooden building used for indoor drying of corn
parole.testo: Probably from Finnish riihi (“kiln, grain drying cabin”).

parole.significato: crosswalk, pedestrian crossing
parole.testo: Compound of skydd (“protection, shelter”) + väg (“road”). Calque of Finnish suojatie.

parole.significato: Nordic walking, walking with ski poles for a full-body exercise
parole.testo: From stav (“staff, pole, ski pole”) + gång (“walking”), calque of Finnish sauvakävely. This training exercise was developed in the 1980s, but SAOB also mentions this word as used since 1652 as a now obsolete synonym to rågång (“borderline between properties and parishes”).

parole.significato: to kill
parole.testo: Literally, “take cabbage on”, associated with chopping of cabbage. May be of Finnish origin (compare kola vippen). Related to Danish gøre kål på (“destroy, kill”), Norwegian Bokmål gjøre kål på and Norwegian Nynorsk gjera kål på (“destroy, finish off”), both said to be originally in sense of making

parole.significato: cooperated voluntary work, often combined with food
parole.testo: From Finnish talkoot.

parole.significato: mandatory teaching of the Swedish language as a subject in Finnish schools
parole.testo: Calque of Finnish pakkoruotsi.
